case_text:
Vignette:
A 30-year-old man presents with a 1-week history of mildly itchy, erythematous patches on both hands. He recently switched to a new laundry detergent approximately two weeks ago. He denies any history of atopic dermatitis, asthma, or food allergies. On examination, there are bilateral, symmetric, well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the dorsal hands with mild scaling. The skin is intact with no cracking, vesicles, or weeping. There is no involvement of the wrists or forearms. He works as an accountant and reports no occupational chemical exposures.
